run.target: Web Admin JWT convergence to a server-owned httpOnly session cookie

rows.action: Sign in through the real login form and reload an authenticated page
rows.assertion: The browser receives an httpOnly SameSite=Lax __session cookie, remains signed in after reload, and has no JWT material in localStorage or sessionStorage

rows.action: Renew and end the server-owned session
rows.assertion: Renewal returns no-store without exposing a JWT; logout removes the cookie and protected routes require login

rows.action: Migrate a valid pre-cookie browser JWT exactly once
rows.assertion: The BFF validates the bearer token, sets __session, and deletes all legacy auth keys without placing the token in a URL or response body

rows.action: Handle invalid and temporarily unexchangeable legacy JWTs
rows.assertion: Invalid tokens are deleted after rejection, while transient network failures preserve the token for a later retry

rows.action: Terminate social-login JWT exchange at the BFF
rows.assertion: The social callback sets an httpOnly session and browser-visible JSON contains no JWT, including an unexpected upstream error envelope
CSR context never reads storage or returns a token, and fetch relies on same-origin credentials without Authorization

rows.action: Download commands and Gerber artifacts through cookie authentication
rows.assertion: Direct fetch call sites send credentials and do not obtain JWTs from browser storage

rows.action: Serialize authenticated loader and AuthContext data to the browser
rows.assertion: Route data and user serialization omit the JWT; AuthContext exposes token as null

rows.action: Sweep production browser code for legacy token storage access
rows.assertion: No localStorage/sessionStorage JWT access remains outside the one-release migration boundary
Exact same-origin writes pass through forwarded proxy headers and a hostile Origin receives 403

rows.action: Preserve explicit bearer API clients without weakening cookie CSRF checks
rows.assertion: Safe methods and explicit Authorization clients bypass ambient-cookie Origin enforcement; cookie mutations do not

rows.action: Audit SSE and WebSocket connection URLs for token query parameters
rows.assertion: No token, access_token, or jwt query construction exists in production Web Admin code

rows.action: Log proxied authentication traffic without token material
rows.assertion: Authorization is fully redacted and response previews replace JWT values with [REDACTED] while forwarded bytes remain unchanged

rows.action: Preserve full proxied response bytes while sanitizing diagnostics
rows.assertion: Log redaction does not truncate or rewrite the response delivered to the caller

rows.action: Keep the migration exchange same-origin and non-cacheable
rows.assertion: Cross-origin migration is rejected and a successful exchange returns 204 with Cache-Control: no-store

residualGaps: The full OSS regular project was run and is not green; the post-fix diagnostic showed the JWT CSRF cluster removed but exposed independent-application tests in the OSS denominator and other pre-existing baseline failures.
The OSS deep project was not run because the blocking regular project remained red.
Legacy browser-token migration is intentionally a one-release compatibility bridge and must be removed in a later release after the migration window closes.
